newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Upbeat Australian stocks bound to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Upbeat Australian stocks bound to higher close.

text.p: The Australian share market closed off its highs for the day but had still locked away solid gains by the close on Thursday as local traders took the bullish lead from record-breaking runs in offshore markets.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 23.3 points to 2,669.7, having peaked late morning at 2,683.7 before sellers succumbed to the temptation to cash in some quick gains.

"It's all been quite firm. We seem to have followed Wall Street again," said broker Robert Cameron of Cameron Securities. A resurgent banking sector was one of best performers on the day, a stronger bond market helping boost the popular group.
ANZ Bank ended with the best gains of the big four, up 1.7 percent to A$9.95 (US$7.36), while Westpac Banking Corp also made good ground, climbing 1.1 percent to A$7.88.
Commonwealth Bank touched a record high at A$16.56 before easing to end up 14.5 cents at A$16.475, while sector heavyweight National Australia Bank rose 14 to A$19.26.
"The banking sector has returned to favour after a bit of profit-taking earlier in the week," said Burrell and Co director, Derek Bond.

Centaur Mining and Exploration NL, controlled by mining entrepreneur Joseph Gutnick, added over 5.6 percent to A$1.50 amid rumours of an imminent bid for Great Central Mines, the largest Gutnick firm.

Great Central Mines, the centre of bid speculation with Canadian giant Barrick Gold Corp, ended seven cents lower at A$2.64 after hitting an early high of A$2.812, 34 percent higher than last week's low of A$2.10 after the bullion selloff.
Great Central's Jundee neighbour in Western Australia Eagle Mining NL made strong gains, up nearly seven percent to A$2.30.

Pay TV operator Australis Media also made strong gains, ending 5.5 cents higher at 20 cents. Traders speculated that an announcement of a long mooted merger with rival operator Foxtel, jointly owned by News Corp and Telstra Corp, the government owned telecommunications carrier, may be imminent.
Automation software group Ci Technologies made a strong debut, ending at A$2.10, 60 cents up on its A$1.50 issue price.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
